Task prompt
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, half of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 4, 1.50x; next round 2.00x):
   10 words: public 1.75, private 0.44
   25 words: public 2.15, private 0.54
   50 words: public 2.84, private 0.71
  100 words: public 4.38, private 1.09
  200 words: public 8.00, private 2.00
  400 words: public 17.50, private 4.38
  800 words: public 45.50, private 11.38
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 6, 2.50x; next round 3.00x):
   10 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
   25 words: public 3.58, private 0.90
   50 words: public 4.74, private 1.18
  100 words: public 7.29, private 1.82
  200 words: public 13.33, private 3.33
  400 words: public 29.17, private 7.29
  800 words: public 75.83, private 18.96
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 1, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 8.00; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, half of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 8, 3.50x; next round 4.00x):

  200 words: public 18.67, private 4.67
  400 words: public 40.83, private 10.21
  800 words: public 106.17, private 26.54
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 1.29; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, half of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices during this trial (1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
This is a trial turn: prices are 1x whatever the round, and you also get a trial-only budget of 2.00, spent before your regular budget. Unspent trial budget is lost when this turn ends, but don't speak just to use it up: say nothing if you have nothing to add.
Your public message this turn is free up to 150 words; beyond that you pay only for the extra length.
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You are on trial. Defend yourself; you speak first. This turn is only for discussion: after everyone has spoken, all players vote Guilty/Innocent in a separate, simultaneous vote.

Task prompt
It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.17; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, half of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.
